questions.def: "Although" introduces a concessive adverbial clause contrasting with the main clause.
questions.question: ___ the evidence was compelling, the jury remained deadlocked.

questions.def: "Despite" is a preposition taking a noun phrase; "failures" is that phrase.
questions.question: He persisted ___ his initial failures.

questions.def: "Even though" introduces a concessive adverbial clause of unexpectedness.
questions.question: The match was cancelled ___ it was still sunny.

questions.def: "Even though" introduces a concessive adverbial clause.
questions.question: ___ he had studied diligently, he failed the exam.

questions.def: "As soon as" indicates immediate succession in an adverbial clause of time.
questions.question: The experiment will commence ___ the equipment arrives.

questions.def: "After finishing" forms a reduced adverbial clause of time.
questions.question: I will call you ___ I my work.

questions.def: "As if" introduces an adverbial clause of manner, often implying unreality.
questions.question: He spoke ___ he knew the answer.

questions.def: "Despite" is a preposition showing contrast.
questions.question: ___ the storm, the ship sailed smoothly.

questions.def: Use "as well as" or "as skillfully as", not "as good as" to modify "sings."
questions.question: She sings as good as her sister does.

questions.def: "Even though" introduces a concessive clause, showing unexpected persistence.
questions.question: He persisted ___ he had failed many times.

questions.def: "However + adjective" introduces a concessive adverbial clause.
questions.question: ___ it may seem, this is the only solution.

questions.def: "As if" introduces a clause of manner, often contrary to fact.
questions.question: She acted ___ nothing had happened.

questions.def: "Had I known" is an inversion expressing a conditional adverbial clause.
questions.question: ___ better, I would have acted differently.

questions.def: "By the time" sets a deadline for the action in the main clause.
questions.question: ___ late, the show had already begun.

questions.def: "Despite" introduces a contrast with the main clause.
questions.question: ___ being warned, he proceeded carelessly.

questions.def: "Weather permitting" forms a reduced adverbial clause of condition.
questions.question: ___, the experiment will proceed.

questions.def: "Should" inversion makes the conditional more formal.
questions.question: ___, I will inform you immediately.

questions.def: "As though" indicates the manner of the action.
questions.question: He spoke eloquently, ___ he had rehearsed for hours.

questions.def: "Had I been invited" is the correct inversion for a past conditional.
questions.question: ___, I would have attended the conference.

questions.def: Inversion with "had" creates a conditional clause.
questions.question: ___, I would have known the truth.

questions.def: "As soon as" indicates immediacy.
questions.question: I will contact you ___ I receive the information.

questions.def: "As if she knew" creates a clause of manner.
questions.question: She behaves ___ everything.

questions.def: "Adjective + as" is a formal way to express concession.
questions.question: ___ she is, she manages to succeed.

questions.def: "Despite" introduces a contrasting element.
questions.question: The results were unexpected, ___ the meticulous planning.

questions.def: 'Given that' introduces a reason for the cancellation, indicating cause.
questions.question: ___ the rain stopped, the match was cancelled.

questions.def: 'Notwithstanding' introduces a contrast to a previous statement.
questions.question: ___ he had promised, he failed to deliver the report.

questions.def: 'Having left' introduces a completed action before the main clause action.
questions.question: ___ the building, he realised he forgot his keys.

questions.def: 'Regardless of' indicates that something does not affect an action.
questions.question: He proceeded with the experiment ___ the risks involved.

questions.def: 'Notwithstanding it' introduces a contrast to what is expected.
questions.question: ___ being a challenging task, she completed it efficiently.

questions.def: 'In that' is used incorrectly; use 'Because' or 'Since' instead.
questions.question: In that he was late, he missed the briefing.
